name: Superfluid IDA forged callAgreement context
summary: Superfluid agreements decoded the ctx bytes from caller-shaped call data without checking the host's ctx stamp. Through Host.callAgreement the attacker passed a forged context naming victims as msgSender, created and updated IDA indexes as those accounts, distributed their super-token balances to itself and downgraded them.
notes: The defect is AgreementLibrary.authorizeTokenAccess, inlined in the IDA, accepting a ctx the host had not stamped; the host and IDA implementations changed in the same reset transaction, so the age does not depend on which carries it.

The anchor forged ctx to create and approve indexes as victims; the campaign transaction distributed and downgraded their balances. A trace scan of all host/IDA transactions from block 24,670,000 to the fix upgrade found no other callAgreement with a non-empty ctx placeholder.
QI (DefiLlama prices it as BENQI), MOCA, SDT, STACK and sdam3CRV are valued at the attacker's realised WETH proceeds (rule 12); USDC.e at par; WETH and MATIC at market.
